author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell Brand reacts to Andrew Tate's declaration that he intends to run for Prime Minister of the UK and makes a genuinely surprising case for why some of Tate's qualities could actually serve the country well. Russell points to the CEO of Rumble's assessment of Tate as a brilliant problem solver with a rare genius for cutting through complexity and argues that beneath the controversy there may be a mind that British politics desperately needs. Not an endorsement of everything Tate stands for but an honest conversation about whether the establishment's most hated outsider might have something real to offer.
